lead: A neighbourhood of housing estates with a very strong community identity and several parks.
text: Until the 19th century it was an almost uninhabited rural area, part of Santa Eulàlia de Vilapicina, and it was developed mainly in the second half of the 20th century with large housing estates for immigrants, especially from the south of Spain. The City Council attributes its name to Pasqual Porta Margarit, a teacher and head of the Colegio Peninsular, who is said to have owned land in Can Porta.

It has a strong sense of its own identity: its residents' association was founded in 1974 and its community movement was very active between 1977 and 1980. Its landmarks include Plaça de Sóller, the Parc de Can Dragó, the Sant Andreu cemetery, Plaça de la República and the Heron City shopping centre. With 31,199 inhabitants in 0.84 km², it is the most populous neighbourhood in the district.
housing: Residential blocks built in the second half of the 20th century, with a farmhouse (masia) here and there recalling the rural past.
